relevance_note: The paper describes 16 people with HA20, an inherited disease associated with loss‐of‐function variants of TNFAIP3 (Sixteen patients from 6 families of European ancestry with HA20 were studied), with per-patient clinical data, so identifiable in-scope individuals are described.
method_note: Read only the paper, schema_ha20_v5.json, extraction_rules_v1.md and extract_v6.md. Spans were located with a script matching short patterns against the paper file, so each span is character-identical to the Markdown (the converter uses U+2010 hyphens, e.g. in auto‐antibodies and loss‐of‐function). Labels: the 16 patients appear only in Table 2, whose first column is a bare-number column (Patient number), so they are labelled Table 2 #<value>. No individual is called a proband or index case, so is_proband is null. No relative is described. Table 2 columns, left to right: Patient number, Family, History of mouth ulcers, History of Genital ulcers, History of gut symptoms, History of colitis/gut ulcers, Liver disease, GI symptoms on collection day, Colchicine on collection day, Other DMARDs on collection day. The table codes 0/1 with no legend, so per the v3 table-symbol rule the 0 cells were left as not reported (never used as exclusions) and the 1 cells were read as the paper's own statement of presence for that person; the text counts corroborate the coding (13 with genital ulcers, 13 with abdominal symptoms, 5 taking colchicine, 6 on immunosuppressants, all 16 with mouth ulcers). No clinical table cell uses a slash-separated stacked value, so D-31 changed nothing here. Variants: the paper states the patients have HA20 and that mutational status was recorded, but prints no variant description anywhere, including the supplement (Table S1 is bacterial taxonomy, Table S2 pathway names), so the 16 variant rows are kept with variant_original_string not reported (D-22). Zygosity, variant type and pathogenicity are not reported because only general disease-level statements are given. Discrepancies: Table 1 gives Colitis 4 (25) and Gastrointestinal ulcer 7 (44) (11 patients), whereas the Table 2 column History of colitis/gut ulcers has 8 ones, and the text says abdominal symptoms in 13 patients. The 5 MRI patients, the patients with available histology (liver 1, stomach 3, ileum 1, colon 4) and the patient in the Discussion treated with TNF-alpha are never identified by label, so their findings were not attributed to any individual; the MRI group statement about hepatic/portal veins and bile ducts was likewise not attributed. Checklist: autoantibodies (ANA/other) stays not reported for everyone because the paper excludes only auto‐antibodies specific to PSC (a narrower feature, kept as an excluded phenotypic feature); the interferon signature is not CRP/ESR, so elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR) stays not reported. cohort_size_as_stated = 38 (16 HA20 patients plus 22 healthy controls, as stated in the abstract); the controls are outside the scope and get no rows. Three families were previously described (^11, ^12, ^13) but the paper does not say which, so source_reference_in_review is not reported for all.
